(5) qa.coupon1792775586@example.com registered 17:13:07 got the daily notice at 17:16:09 (marker daily:<date>:<id>), no restart needed. (6) No cancel buttons on past preview entries. (7) FR/ES scan of the landing page and 12 app pages (overview, number overview/forwarding/hours/ivr/voicemail/billing, extra-number billing, wallet, quick-call, inbox, buy) found no remaining UI English except the intentional or content items below. 'Salut Alice'/'Hola Alice', 'Tester mon numéro'/'Appeler mon numéro', 'Probar mi número'/'Llamar a mi número', route summary, LLAMADAS/APPELS, 'Horaires'/'Horario', pricing-extra-usage full sentence, 'Numéro vert'/'Número gratuito' and mobile bottom nav 'Accueil' are all translated. (8) At 390px in fr and es: no horizontal overflow on quick-call, settings, billing/ivr/voicemail tabs, campaigns/new or buy. (9) Switching from es to en via topbar-lang-switcher restores English. AI chat answered a how-to question, and 'talk to a human' shows support-chat-human-link-3 → t.me/onarrival1 (2 OpenAI messages used). Quick IVR transfer returns the preview result. State restored: Alice main on Business $120, recording on, downgradeSaved []; Bob ivrTrialUsed=false.

ui_bugs.issue: React warning 'Cannot infer the option value of complex children' is still logged (an <option> has mixed children without a value prop). The '<span> cannot be a child of <tbody>/<tr>' hydration warnings also remain; they likely come from the visual-edit tooling.

design_issues.screen: Remaining English in FR/ES (content-like, judge whether to translate)
issues: IVR tab greeting textarea (ivr-greeting-text-input) is prefilled with 'Thank you for calling. Please select an option.' when no IVR is saved (Alice's ivr is undefined), so it is a default prefill, not user text. Consider a localized default.
Overview activity shows 'Is the shop open on Sunday?' and the '“Hi, this is Dana from Acme…”' voicemail transcript. These are seeded SMS/voicemail content (intentional).
Voicemail sample 'The person at … is unavailable…' follows the selected greeting language (intentional).
ES number tab 'Recording' is translated as 'Grabando' ('recording in progress'); 'Grabación' would be more natural.

With ?tab=billing the horizontal tab strip does not scroll to show the active tab. The visible tabs are Accueil/Renvoi/Horaires/IVR, so the user cannot see which tab is active. Consider scrollIntoView on the active tab.

Asked 'How do I schedule a Quick IVR call?', the AI says Quick IVR calls are on Pro and Business, but it does not mention that scheduling is Business-only (the UI shows 'Scheduling, presets and redial are on the Business plan'). Consider adding this to the support prompt's knowledge.

action_items: LOW: give the <option> with complex children a value prop or a plain string to silence the React warning
LOW: localize the default IVR greeting prefill, or leave it empty with a translated placeholder
LOW: ES 'Grabando' → 'Grabación' for the Recording tab
LOW: on mobile, scroll the active number tab into view
LOW: support AI prompt: scheduling/presets/redial are Business-only
critical_code_review_comments: extras.js announceCoupon loads all webAccounts and tries an insertOne per account every 5 minutes (duplicate-key errors for the ones already sent). That is fine at the current scale, but it is O(accounts) DB writes every run; consider a bulk query of the markers that already exist, or filtering by createdAt > the last run.

numbers.js upgrade restores downgradeSaved values blindly. If the user changed the same setting in between (only possible for features still allowed on the lower plan), the saved value would overwrite it. Today all saved keys are gated on the lower plan, so this is OK.
